Labor includes: taking care of plants, cleaning walkways, cleaning elevators, cleaning the laundry room, etc. The CO-OP has 3 sections, which is why we're called the Super Co-op. The first and second floors are Laurel, the third is Nueces, and the fourth and fifth are Halstead. Nueces is the only section of the building where rooms have their own kitchen, and everyone has their own restroom. All the other floors have a communal kitchen, and as part of their labor, they also have to cook for everyone else, depending on what's on the menu. All of it is student ran so there is drama, but we do report to a main office.

Windtree Condominiums.text: I like having my own bathroom, it's also just a 5min walk from the CPE

Yugo Austin Corner.text: Decent apartment. The only downside to living here was in the fall semester when the elevator would go out all the time and we lived on the top floor. They have gotten a new contractor who seems to have really turned things around elevaor wise. It may seem far from campus but the bus stop is right outside your door. Doesn't have a gym of dedicated study rooms (only a little area in the lobby) and I know there are places that go for around the same rate with gyms. Also really nice if you're a cyclist because they have a dedicated bike cage in the parking garage. Plus if you're a dog owner they have their own closed off dog park in the back.
expensive parking, far from campus (for wampus)

Yugo Austin Rio.text: Close to campus, elevators sometimes malfunction, includes gym
Management is lowkey annoying. Maintenance doesn't knock on room doors before entering.

Yugo Austin Waterloo.text: $35 a month green fee, great amenities (rooftop pool 30 floors high, gym, yoga room, saunas, cycling room, study area 2nd floor, free printing, Luxer package delivery system, refrigerators in mail room for grocery deliveries), however my first semester here we went down to 2 elevators out of the 4 in the building operational after just a week or two into the Fall semester. Being on the 25th floor made calling for an elevator extremely difficult with long wait times before seeing an elevator. By the time the elevator picked up people from floors 30-20 it was more or less full making people on lower floors have to wait even longer to get in an empty elevator. Additionally at times it would be down to 1 elevator because one of the elevators out of the 2 was getting overworked with the reduced elevator capacity making management slow down that elevator. Eventually they were fixed after 3 months (December) and have been fine ever since but definitely not a good elevator experience the first half of the year.
